articles.title: Rising or persistently high HPV levels may signal greater cervical precancer risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Among women with persistent HPV infection, rising or consistently high viral loads were associated with greater cervical precancer or cancer risk. The finding may help refine monitoring, but it does not establish viral load as a stand-alone diagnostic test.

articles.title: How do tumors talk to nerves? This scientist is finding out
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researcher Sebnem Ece Eksi identified memory-related proteins in prostate cancer cells and is investigating nerve fibers within tumors. The work seeks to clarify how tumors and nerves communicate.

articles.title: Alcohol may weaken cancer immunotherapy, early research suggests
articles.summary_3_sentences: Early research examined whether regular alcohol consumption can reduce the effectiveness of cancer immunotherapy. The finding is preliminary and should not be treated as proof of a clinical effect in all patients.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.summary_3_sentences: An AI tool identified patterns associated with bladder cancer as long as five years before diagnosis and detected 85% of cases in a study of nearly 70,000 patients. Further validation is needed before clinical screening use.

articles.title: FDA Approves GSK Treatment for ALK-Positive Lung Cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA granted accelerated approval to neladalkib, marketed as Nelkarmi, for ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer. The record does not provide further details about the approved population or supporting trial.

articles.title: 'Pan-RAS molecular glue' is a safe and effective treatment for lung and pancreatic cancers
articles.summary_3_sentences: In the Phase I AURORAS-1 trial, the pan-RAS molecular glue ERAS-0015 was reported to be safe and to shrink some lung and pancreatic tumors. These are early clinical findings requiring confirmation in larger trials.

articles.title: Commonly used drug kills leukemia cells early by acting mainly on RNA, not DNA
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research suggests that azacitidine initially kills leukemia cells mainly through effects on RNA rather than the DNA mechanism traditionally emphasized. The mechanistic finding may refine understanding of a treatment used for MDS and AML.

articles.title: Metastatic pancreatic cancer responds well to treatment with combination of daraxonrasib and chemotherapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: Daraxonrasib plus chemotherapy produced substantial tumor shrinkage in patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer in a Phase I/II trial. The early-stage results require confirmation in larger comparative studies.

articles.title: Protein Patterns Predict Immunotherapy Response in Melanoma
articles.summary_3_sentences: Protein patterns were reported to distinguish melanoma patients according to their response to immunotherapy. Such patterns could potentially support treatment selection, although the record provides no validation details.

articles.title: Novel Inflammatory Protein Drives Pancreatic Cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified an inflammatory protein described as a driver of pancreatic cancer. The finding is mechanistic, and the supplied record does not establish a clinical treatment based on the protein.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden hereditary form of aggressive prostate cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: A rare inherited CDK12 mutation was linked to aggressive prostate cancer, with all five identified carriers developing metastatic disease between ages 44 and 62. The small number of carriers means the result needs broader confirmation.

articles.title: Nanoplastics Linked to Colorectal Cancer in New Study
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports a study linking nanoplastics with colorectal cancer. The supplied excerpt contains too little information to characterize the study design, mechanism, or strength of the association.

articles.title: FDA Declines Approval of Novel Bispecific Lung Cancer Therapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA declined to approve a bispecific lung cancer therapy developed by Summit Therapeutics. The record does not state the agency's rationale or the treatment's clinical data.

articles.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A mathematical model suggests vitamin C taken after meals could reduce formation of potentially carcinogenic compounds from nitrates and nitrites in the stomach. This modeling result does not yet demonstrate cancer prevention in people.

articles.title: Common forever chemicals linked to nearly double the rate of aggressive breast cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: An NIH study associated high levels of two PFAS chemicals with up to 93% higher rates of an aggressive breast cancer subtype. The observational association does not by itself prove that the chemicals caused the cancers.

articles.title: Colorectal cancer is rising again after 20 years, and scientists don't know why
articles.summary_3_sentences: A U.S. study found colorectal cancer rates rising across nearly every age group under 70 after more than two decades of decline. The reasons for the renewed increase remain unclear.

articles.title: Scientists discover a common sugar may help cancer cells break free and spread
articles.summary_3_sentences: Preclinical experiments suggest that fructose released by chemotherapy-surviving ovarian cancer cells can weaken cell adhesion and facilitate spread. Effects involving dietary fructose and statins were also reported, but human clinical relevance remains unproven.

articles.title: Cancer-fighting chewing gum slashes HPV levels by up to 93%
articles.summary_3_sentences: A bioengineered chewing-gum extract reduced HPV levels by up to 93% in oral samples from cancer patients and suppressed two harmful bacterial species. These sample-based findings do not yet show that chewing the gum prevents or treats cancer.

articles.title: Hormone Inhibitors Combined with Surgery Reduce Prostate Tumor Progression
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that combining hormone inhibitors with surgery reduced prostate tumor progression. The supplied text does not provide trial design, effect size, or patient-selection details.

articles.title: Novel Tri-therapy Improves Treatment Outcomes in Patients with Gastric Cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: A three-part therapy was reported to improve outcomes in patients with gastric cancer. The record does not specify the regimen, comparison group, or magnitude of benefit.

articles.title: A simple supplement may help clear brain fog after cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: Breast cancer survivors taking oxaloacetate for eight weeks reported improvements in memory, concentration, mental clarity, and fatigue. Larger controlled studies are needed to establish effectiveness and safety.

articles.title: MIT scientists turn immune cells into cancer killers inside the body
articles.summary_3_sentences: Nanoparticles reprogrammed immune cells inside mice, eliminating tumors and reversing liver damage in experiments. The approach remains preclinical and has not been shown to work safely in humans.

articles.title: Scientists trick cancer cells into making the drugs that kill them
articles.summary_3_sentences: Laboratory researchers used carbon monoxide produced by tumor cells to generate active drugs within the cancer cells themselves. The strategy is experimental and has not yet demonstrated safety or efficacy in patients.

articles.title: Scientists finally discover how a common gut bacterium can trigger colon cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that a toxin from Bacteroides fragilis damages the colon's protective lining, promotes inflammation, and supports tumor formation. The mechanistic work helps explain an association between the bacterium and colorectal cancer.

articles.title: Novel Mechanism of Wound Healing Helps Tumors Evade Immunity
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a wound-healing mechanism that helps tumors avoid immune recognition. The mechanistic finding may inform future immunotherapy research, but no clinical intervention is described.

articles.title: Why some “lower-risk” childhood cancers turn deadly
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found hidden aggressive cells in some childhood rhabdomyosarcomas previously classified as lower risk. The finding could improve risk stratification and help tailor chemotherapy intensity.

articles.title: A Dual Immunotherapy Approach for Treating Lung Cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article examines dual immunotherapy for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer, a disease with poor outcomes. The supplied record does not state the treatment combination or trial results.

articles.title: Researcher examines how blood vessel damage relates to memory loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research is examining how damage to brain blood vessels may contribute to memory loss alongside Alzheimer's-related processes. The work highlights vascular health as a potentially important component of cognitive decline.

articles.title: Type 2 diabetes linked to 53% higher Alzheimer’s risk, major review finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A review of 40 studies associated type 2 diabetes with a 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's disease. The result identifies an epidemiological association rather than proving that diabetes directly causes Alzheimer's.

articles.title: New structures come into view in brain wiring maps
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers accelerated an imaging technique enough to map large volumes of brain tissue at nanoscale resolution. The method reveals structures that conventional connectome maps can miss.

articles.title: Alzheimer’s breakthrough exposes a hidden flaw in the brain’s cleanup system
articles.summary_3_sentences: A gene was found to help brain immune cells contain plaques associated with Alzheimer's disease. When the gene malfunctioned in mice, plaque buildup and cognitive decline accelerated, making the finding preclinical.

articles.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that AI models capable of predicting brain activity may rely on internal processes unlike those used by the brain. The result cautions against assuming predictive similarity reflects biological similarity.

articles.title: Improved mapping reveals location of small molecules in the brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: A new methodology maps small molecules in the brain and distinguishes molecules with nearly identical structures. It may improve spatial analysis of brain chemistry.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden eye disease that slowly steals night vision
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified a genetic eye disorder that progressively impairs night and peripheral vision while sparing central vision for years. Difficulty adapting to darkness may provide an early warning sign.

articles.title: This simple habit is linked to a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's
articles.summary_3_sentences: Reading for pleasure has been associated with lower stress, better cognition, and a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease. These associations do not establish that reading itself prevents dementia.

articles.title: The brain's protective barrier also blocks medicine. This engineer wants a way through
articles.summary_3_sentences: Engineer Rebecca Pinals developed a blood-brain barrier model on a chip to study drug delivery to the brain. The platform is intended to support research on treatments for dementia and other neurological diseases.

articles.title: Is free will an illusion? New brain research reveals a surprising twist
articles.summary_3_sentences: Brain activity was found to build toward both freely chosen and forced decisions through similar neural processes. The study suggests that preferences and experience may still shape choices despite shared decision mechanisms.

articles.title: Ozempic and Mounjaro may have a surprising effect on your brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Observational evidence has linked GLP-1 drugs with lower dementia risk, but major trials found semaglutide did not slow established Alzheimer's disease. Any cognitive benefit may depend on population and timing and remains uncertain.

articles.title: Tiny magnets deep inside the brain could transform Parkinson’s treatment
articles.summary_3_sentences: Magnetic nanoparticles were used to stimulate deep brain regions and improve Parkinson's-like movement problems in mice. The technique remains preclinical and would require extensive safety testing before human use.

articles.title: Investigating APOE4, an Alzheimer's Risk Gene, and Oligodendrocyte Function
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research examined how the Alzheimer's risk variant APOE4 affects oligodendrocyte function. The work describes a possible cellular pathway through which the variant may impair brain function.

articles.title: A hidden biological divide may help explain Alzheimer’s and chronic pain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research highlighted differences by biological sex, genetics, and menopause in Alzheimer's risk, treatment response, and chronic pain. Immune and gut-brain differences may eventually support more personalized approaches.

articles.title: MIT scientists discover a surprising way to boost the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
articles.summary_3_sentences: Carefully timed pink-noise bursts during sleep strengthened brain waves associated with waste clearance. Whether this approach prevents memory decline or Alzheimer's disease has not yet been established.

articles.title: A little-known protein could be a powerful weapon against Alzheimer’s
articles.summary_3_sentences: Increasing SORLA reduced tau tangles, protected neural connections, and limited brain shrinkage in mice. The results identify a potential target but remain preclinical.

articles.title: MIT discovers that aging weakens the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
articles.summary_3_sentences: The brain's sleep-related waste-removal activity was found to weaken with age alongside changes in deep-sleep waves and blood flow. Some older adults retained stronger patterns similar to those of younger people.

articles.title: An ancient virus may help explain what makes the human brain different
articles.summary_3_sentences: Ancient viral DNA in the chimpanzee genome appears to suppress LINC00662, a gene active in humans and implicated in early brain development. The finding offers a possible evolutionary mechanism for developmental differences.

articles.title: Alzheimer’s may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: Brain imaging indicated that two regions involved in memory and emotion may shrink before the hippocampus and as long as a decade before memory symptoms. The changes were associated with abnormal tau accumulation.

articles.title: Altered Gene Expression Drives Alzheimer's Disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article links altered gene expression with mechanisms underlying Alzheimer's disease. The supplied record does not identify the genes, experimental model, or clinical implications.

articles.title: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer’s years before symptoms
articles.summary_3_sentences: Patterns of brain activity were reported to predict Alzheimer's risk before memory symptoms and to identify unusually resilient brains. Prospective validation is needed before use as a clinical predictor.

articles.title: A surprising brain difference may explain why some kids struggle with math
articles.summary_3_sentences: Children with developmental dyscalculia showed difficulty switching problem-solving strategies and adapting to changing task demands. Distinct brain-activity patterns were associated with these mathematical difficulties.

articles.title: Science to restore speech is moving fast. Here's what's next
articles.summary_3_sentences: Neurotechnology is being developed to restore fluent speech for people who can no longer talk. The article reviews the field's progress and the patients who may benefit.

articles.title: High-Dose Flu Vaccine Linked to Lower Alzheimer's Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: High-dose influenza vaccination in older adults was associated with a lower risk of Alzheimer's disease. The association does not prove that the vaccine prevents neurodegeneration.

articles.title: Common osteoporosis drugs linked to 24% lower dementia risk in major study
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of more than 120,000 older adults associated common osteoporosis drugs with up to a 24% lower risk of dementia. The observational result does not establish a protective drug effect.

articles.title: Alzheimer’s may have early warning signs outside the brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Human-cell laboratory models showed that inherited Alzheimer's mutations can disrupt nerve-to-muscle connections without involvement of the brain or spinal cord. The mechanistic finding may relate to early movement changes but is not yet a diagnostic test.

articles.title: Drinking 2–3 cups of coffee a day linked to dramatically lower dementia risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Long-term consumption of two to three cups of caffeinated coffee daily was associated with lower dementia risk and better cognition. Decaffeinated coffee did not show the same association, and causality was not established.

articles.title: Stronger flu shot linked to nearly 55% lower Alzheimer's risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: An analysis of nearly 200,000 older adults associated high-dose influenza vaccination with an almost 55% lower Alzheimer's risk. The observational finding does not prove a preventive effect.

articles.title: Scientists discover hidden brain changes linked to common sleep disorders
articles.summary_3_sentences: A review of 57 imaging studies linked sleep disorders with structural differences in brain regions involved in attention, decisions, and emotion. Both shared and disorder-specific patterns were reported.

articles.title: Magic mushrooms rewire the brain in a way scientists didn't expect
articles.summary_3_sentences: Psilocybin rapidly altered and strengthened neural connections in mice, with different effects in healthy and chronically stressed animals. Researchers also triggered some rewiring without the associated behavioral response, but the work remains preclinical.

articles.title: An anti-aging drug may help protect the brain before Alzheimer's symptoms begin
articles.summary_3_sentences: Four weeks of low-dose rapamycin improved brain blood flow in healthy middle-aged APOE4 carriers, with stronger effects reported in women. The short study does not show that rapamycin prevents Alzheimer's disease.

articles.title: Scientists may have finally explained why our brains and bodies are cross-wired
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers propose that the brain's cross-wiring originated in ancient fish visual systems more than 500 million years ago. The arrangement may be an evolutionary legacy rather than a later adaptation with a specific advantage.

articles.title: Scientists identify two overlooked skills that predict reading success
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large study found that sound recognition, vocabulary, and background knowledge were stronger predictors of children's reading success than intelligence or visual processing. The findings may inform support for struggling readers.

articles.title: The brain’s hidden fear mechanism may explain anxiety and PTSD
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, fear caused neural representations of dangerous and safe environments to overlap. The preclinical mechanism may help explain fear generalization in anxiety and PTSD but has not been demonstrated directly in patients.

articles.title: Scientists discover new Alzheimer’s drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
articles.summary_3_sentences: A drug originally developed for spinal cord injury was reported to reduce DNA damage and inflammation relevant to Alzheimer's disease. Although the compound has undergone initial human safety testing, efficacy for Alzheimer's remains unestablished.

articles.title: Scientists discover mysterious “lonely” brain waves linked to memory loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: Disrupted deep-sleep brain waves were linked with Alzheimer's-related protein accumulation and memory loss. The findings suggest that altered overnight memory processing may precede symptoms.

articles.title: Extra weight may be aging your brain faster than you think
articles.summary_3_sentences: A 24-year study of more than 8,200 adults associated excess body weight with faster decline in memory, concentration, and decision-making. The relationship was strongest among adults older than 65.

articles.title: Common pesticide linked to 2.5 times the risk of Parkinson’s disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Long-term exposure to a common pesticide was associated with more than 2.5 times the risk of Parkinson's disease. Researchers also investigated how the chemical damages brain cells, but the epidemiological association alone does not prove causation.

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising brain benefit of eating peanuts every day
articles.summary_3_sentences: Older adults eating about two servings of unsalted, skin-roasted peanuts daily for 16 weeks showed improved insulin responsiveness in memory-related brain regions. The study does not establish long-term protection from dementia.

articles.title: A simple blood test could reveal Alzheimer’s risk 10 years before symptoms
articles.summary_3_sentences: A blood biomarker test stratified future cognitive-decline risk, with the highest-risk group estimated to have a 78% chance of impairment within 10 years. Clinical utility will require prospective validation.

articles.title: Bladder Cancer Vaccine Reduces Risk of Dementia
articles.summary_3_sentences: Use of BCG, which is administered for bladder cancer and also used as a tuberculosis vaccine, was associated with reduced dementia risk. The record does not establish a causal neuroprotective effect.

articles.title: Six popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: Among nearly 13,000 adults, high consumption of six artificial sweeteners was associated with faster cognitive decline. The observational study did not establish that the sweeteners caused brain aging.

articles.title: A single brain signal may explain schizophrenia's most puzzling symptoms
articles.summary_3_sentences: A weakened brain signal was associated with sensory-processing problems, disorganized speech, and greater schizophrenia severity. The finding may help unify several symptoms under a shared mechanism.

articles.title: The autistic brain processes faces differently than scientists thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: Face-recognition brain signals became more specialized with age in neurotypical children but changed less in autistic children. The finding may help explain some differences in recognizing faces and emotions.

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising clue to why some brains resist Alzheimer’s
articles.summary_3_sentences: Rare immature brain cells remained present in some people older than 80, but their behavior differed between cognitively resilient people and those with dementia. The finding may offer clues about resistance to Alzheimer's pathology.

articles.title: Researchers find teens are more likely to use tobacco, alcohol and marijuana when adults at home smoke or vape
articles.summary_3_sentences: Adolescents living with adults who smoked or vaped were more likely to use tobacco, alcohol, marijuana, and other substances. Risk was highest when both a parent and another household adult used these products.

articles.title: Daily cannabis use surpasses daily drinking among Canadians under 50, survey finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Canadian survey found daily cannabis use now exceeds daily alcohol use among adults younger than 50. Among adults younger than 35, daily cannabis smoking was as common as daily cigarette smoking.

articles.title: Cannabidiol not effective for treating severe behavioral problems in children with intellectual disabilities
articles.summary_3_sentences: A randomized controlled trial found that cannabidiol did not effectively treat severe behavioral problems in children with intellectual disability. The result does not support CBD for this indication.

articles.title: 32% of postpartum women report needing mental health care in survey spanning 16 states
articles.summary_3_sentences: A survey across 16 states found that 32% of postpartum women reported needing mental health care. The result underscores gaps in screening and connection to care after childbirth.

articles.title: Stress and anxiety are wearing workers down: How to spot your triggers and cope
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses workplace stress and anxiety and ways to identify triggers and cope. The supplied summary does not describe a specific study or quantitative finding.

articles.title: Marijuana Use May Raise Stroke & Cardiovascular Disease Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Cannabis use, including occasional use, was associated with greater reported risks of stroke and cardiovascular disease. The association does not prove cannabis directly caused the events.

articles.title: Mental health diagnoses rise with medical complexity, chronicity in children
articles.summary_3_sentences: Among Medicaid-enrolled children, mental health diagnoses became more common as medical complexity and chronicity increased. The study highlights the need for integrated behavioral and medical care.

articles.title: Hair pulling, skin picking and nail biting are common in young people and cause significant distress
articles.summary_3_sentences: Body-focused repetitive behaviors were common and distressing among young people. Distress was particularly prominent among those also experiencing anxiety, depression, or bullying.

articles.title: Alcohol addiction and eating disorders often go hand in hand--here's why
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article examines the overlap between risky drinking and disordered eating, including skipping meals to intensify alcohol's effects or reduce calories. This behavior can compound nutritional and substance-related harms.

articles.title: For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of more than 10,000 college students associated less frequent exercise with greater depression and anxiety one year later. Consistency appeared more relevant than workout intensity or duration, although causality was not established.

articles.title: A study of 30,000 people reveals which antidepressants may work best
articles.summary_3_sentences: A review involving more than 30,000 people found that three antidepressants, including escitalopram and duloxetine, may maintain symptom improvement better than fluoxetine. Study limitations and limited long-term data prevent identifying one best drug.

articles.title: Too much exercise could leave your brain stuck in overdrive
articles.summary_3_sentences: Mice exposed to prolonged intensive training had elevated dopamine in a brain region involved in memory and emotion 48 hours later. The work is preclinical, and symptoms such as anxiety or insomnia were not directly measured.

articles.title: What to know about kratom and its powerful derivatives
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists and toxicologists are warning that some kratom-derived chemicals have strong opioid-like effects. These properties raise concerns about toxicity, dependence, and misuse.

articles.title: The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected
articles.summary_3_sentences: Psychopathic traits were associated with varied language patterns, including more positive language in some people and more negativity or less anxiety in others. The findings challenge simple stereotypes and suggest substantial heterogeneity.

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Finnish longitudinal study found that children with more screen time tended to show better cognitive processing as teenagers. Researchers suggested that the type of screen activity may matter more than total duration.

articles.title: Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.
articles.summary_3_sentences: Average brain activity was similar between autistic and non-autistic groups, but autistic individuals showed much greater person-to-person variation. The heterogeneity was especially marked in regions involved in social understanding.

articles.title: Cannabis addiction linked to 57% higher odds of suicidal thoughts
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a study of more than 415,000 U.S. adults, cannabis use disorder was associated with 57% higher odds of suicidal thoughts. Associations were especially elevated among women and younger adults, but causality was not established.

articles.title: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study reveals a surprising health divide
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of more than 340,000 adults associated moderate wine use with lower cardiovascular mortality, while light beer, cider, or spirits use was associated with higher risk. Heavy drinking was harmful across beverage types, and confounding may explain some differences.

articles.title: New wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery
articles.summary_3_sentences: A wearable ultrasound patch helped participants enter REM sleep sooner and remain in REM longer on average. The early findings also suggested effects on stress-related brain circuits, but broader testing is needed.

articles.title: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression
articles.summary_3_sentences: Older adults with more consistent daily schedules reported less physical pain and fewer depressive symptoms, including among those with insomnia. The observational result may reflect benefits of circadian regularity but does not prove causation.

articles.title: A 19-year study reveals a troubling link between napping and death
articles.summary_3_sentences: Among 1,338 older adults, longer and more frequent naps were associated with higher mortality over as long as 19 years. Morning naps and each additional hour of daytime sleep were also associated with increased risk, but napping may be a marker of underlying illness.

articles.title: Forcing yourself to smile can actually make you miserable
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a study of more than 1,100 participants, one artificial smile produced a small mood benefit, but repeatedly forcing smiles erased or reversed it. The findings suggest emotional effects depend on context and repetition.

articles.title: Energy drinks linked to 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest
articles.summary_3_sentences: Energy drinks and stimulant supplements were disproportionately represented in reports of cardiac arrest and heart attack. Reporting data cannot establish incidence or causation, but the pattern raises safety concerns, especially for young adults.

articles.title: Even occasional marijuana use linked to 40% higher odds of stroke
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study involving more than 440,000 Americans associated occasional cannabis use with 40% higher odds of reporting a stroke history. The cross-sectional association does not prove that marijuana caused stroke.

articles.title: Popular cannabis sleep gummies may have a hidden dark side
articles.summary_3_sentences: Repeated exposure to cannabinol, an ingredient in some sleep gummies, produced tolerance and withdrawal signs in mice. Human dependence and long-term safety remain uncertain.

articles.title: Newly identified transport pathway reveals how caveolin-1 helps cells store fat
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a transport pathway through which caveolin-1 supports fat storage in cells. The mechanistic finding may improve understanding of lipodystrophy and abnormal lipid deposition.

articles.title: Intermittent fasting helps injured muscles regenerate in mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: Alternating fasting and feeding promoted muscle repair-cell proliferation and fusion after injury in mice. The effect depended on a pathway associated with cancer-related muscle wasting and has not been established in humans.

articles.title: A 194-year-old tortoise has a remarkable anti-aging secret hidden in its DNA
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified 287 genetic variants in a 194-year-old giant tortoise linked to DNA repair, inflammation, insulin regulation, and cancer suppression. The study offers comparative clues about longevity rather than a human anti-aging intervention.

articles.title: Despite soaring demand for GLP-1s, many eligible patients are unable to access these drugs for weight loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: Use of GLP-1 receptor agonists has risen rapidly, but access among eligible U.S. patients remains unequal. The study found widening disparities as demand increased.

articles.title: Giving patients a greater voice in their diabetes care
articles.summary_3_sentences: Two studies tested an approach for incorporating patients' priorities into diabetes management. The work focuses on aligning treatment decisions with individual goals and preferences.

articles.title: Common medications may secretly rewire your gut, with effects lasting for years
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of more than 2,500 people found persistent gut-microbiome signatures associated with prior use of several common medications. Some anxiety medications showed effects comparable to broad-spectrum antibiotics, although the study does not prove lasting clinical harm.

articles.title: Upskilling health professionals to deliver emotional well-being support for people with diabetes
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes efforts to train health professionals to provide emotional well-being support for people managing diabetes. The approach recognizes the continuous psychological burden of self-management.

articles.title: Your genes might boost risk for high cholesterol
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study suggests inherited factors may contribute to persistently high cholesterol levels. The supplied summary does not identify the variants or quantify their effects.

articles.title: People respond faster to a sugary drink's logo after three weeks of daily consumption
articles.summary_3_sentences: After drinking a branded high-sugar beverage daily for three weeks, participants responded more quickly to its logo. The cue-related motivation appeared stronger than preference for the drink's taste.

articles.title: Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a clinical trial, a ketogenic diet reduced liver fat more than Mediterranean or low-fat diets despite similar weight loss. Average liver fat fell 67%, and about half of the keto group no longer met prediabetes criteria after four to five months.

articles.title: A common blood pressure drug has a surprising effect on calorie-burning brown fat
articles.summary_3_sentences: A common blood pressure drug activated brown fat in mice. A separate analysis of more than 100,000 patients associated brown fat with lower rates of several metabolic and cardiovascular conditions, but the therapeutic implications remain uncertain.

articles.title: Experimental compound burns fat without sacrificing muscle
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental compound increased energy expenditure, improved glucose control, and reduced liver fat and weight in mice without substantial muscle loss. Combining it with a GLP-1 drug produced greater effects, but the work remains preclinical.

articles.title: Powerful new weight-loss drug helps patients cut knee pain in half
articles.summary_3_sentences: At the highest dose, retatrutide produced about 25% weight loss, while roughly two-thirds of participants reported at least a 50% reduction in knee pain. Whether it prevents structural joint damage remains unknown.

articles.title: Why don't weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy work for everyone?
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers are investigating whether compensatory reductions in energy expenditure help explain variable responses to GLP-1 weight-loss drugs. The work may eventually support more personalized obesity treatment.

articles.title: Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods. Every single one contained fungal toxins
articles.summary_3_sentences: Testing of 212 plant-based foods and drinks sold in the United Kingdom detected at least one mycotoxin in every product. Detection does not necessarily mean levels exceeded safety limits or caused harm.

articles.title: Why obesity affects men and women differently may be hiding in their fat
articles.summary_3_sentences: In mice, immune-cell subtypes in fat had different effects on obesity-related inflammation depending on biological sex. The preclinical study may help explain sex differences in metabolic disease.

articles.title: Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder
articles.summary_3_sentences: Vitamin B12 largely reversed developmental abnormalities in worms carrying a mutation linked to Verheij syndrome. Similar metabolic changes were observed in patients, but clinical benefit from supplementation has not been demonstrated.

articles.title: Fasting Draws on Muscle When Fat Stores Can't be Tapped
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that the body may break down muscle during fasting when it cannot access fat stores. The supplied record does not specify the experimental model or clinical context.

articles.title: Yale scientists reveal what really slows aging and what doesn't
articles.summary_3_sentences: A review of 51 studies found that some prescription drugs, healthy diets, and exercise measurably affected biological-aging markers, while popular supplements generally did not. Changes in biomarkers do not necessarily mean longer life.

articles.title: Scientists finally discover why we learn to love bitter coffee
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a gut-to-brain dopamine pathway that may help people learn to prefer initially bitter flavors such as coffee. The mechanism could inform research on acquired food preferences.

articles.title: AI helps Stanford scientists discover a “natural Ozempic” with a surprising advantage
articles.summary_3_sentences: An AI-identified molecule called BRP reduced food intake and fat mass in animals while preserving muscle and avoiding major digestive effects. The molecule targets a different brain pathway from GLP-1 drugs and remains preclinical.

articles.title: Kids who eat more ultra-processed foods show a troubling brain response
articles.summary_3_sentences: Among 46 children, greater ultra-processed food intake was associated with stronger reward-system responses to tempting food images. Those responses were linked with larger increases in body fat and BMI one year later.

articles.title: Scientists reverse liver cell aging and cut Alzheimer’s-linked protein in half
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental drug rejuvenated liver cells in rats, reduced an Alzheimer's-linked protein, and lowered harmful cholesterol. The findings are preclinical and do not show prevention of Alzheimer's or heart disease in people.

articles.title: New diabetes implant uses electricity to lower blood sugar and promote weight loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: An electrically powered implant converted excess glucose into a substance eliminated in urine, controlling blood sugar and promoting weight loss in diabetic mice. The device remains preclinical.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden driver of high cholesterol and a way to stop it
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a pathway through which a high-cholesterol diet undermines natural cholesterol control, and blocking it lowered LDL in mice. A related experimental drug has passed an early human safety trial, but efficacy remains unproven.

articles.title: Body Composition Correlates with Biological Aging in Men
articles.summary_3_sentences: Body composition was reported to correlate with biological aging in men. The supplied record does not provide measurements or establish whether changing body composition alters aging.

articles.title: Type 2 diabetes breakthrough as 54% achieve remission in just 6 months
articles.summary_3_sentences: Among adults younger than 45, 54% following an intensive low-calorie diet and exercise program achieved type 2 diabetes remission within six months, versus 4% with usual care. Longer follow-up is needed to assess durability.

articles.title: The secret to slower aging may be hiding in your gut
articles.summary_3_sentences: Differences in gut bacteria accounted for an estimated 15% of variation in biological-aging rates. Certain species were associated with slower or faster aging, but the study does not establish a causal effect.

articles.title: Mayo Clinic discovers new ways to fight the “zombie” cells that drive aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: A series of studies examined senescent cells and possible ways to target them, including a tomato-derived compound. Experimental treatments reduced inflammation and improved physical and brain measures in aging mice.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden switch that burns fat and blocks new fat cells
articles.summary_3_sentences: Disabling a protein called Mitch increased fat burning and inhibited formation of new human fat cells in laboratory experiments. Related mouse studies showed resistance to obesity, but no human treatment has been established.

articles.title: Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Older adults who followed a Mediterranean diet more closely had higher levels of the mitochondrial peptides humanin and SHMOOSE. These proteins have been linked to healthy aging, but their role in mediating diet benefits remains uncertain.

articles.title: Unique Protein in Kidneys Regulates Blood Vessel Integrity
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a kidney protein involved in maintaining blood-vessel integrity. The mechanistic finding may be relevant to chronic kidney disease, but no treatment is described.

articles.title: A fast-growing heart is good for the Grinch. People are another story
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article contrasts fictional rapid heart growth with the biological consequences of heart enlargement in people. The supplied record does not provide specific study results.

articles.title: Heart rhythm data reveal early signs of heart disease before conventional measures
articles.summary_3_sentences: Patterns in beat-to-beat variation revealed early effects of inherited cardiomyopathy before conventional measures. The approach may support earlier detection but requires clinical validation.

articles.title: Scientists discover that the heart doesn't age the way we thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: Age-related inflammation and scarring were concentrated in heart valves and major vessels rather than evenly distributed through heart muscle. The finding revises understanding of cardiac aging.

articles.title: Alternative Treatment for Kidney Failure Could Replace Dialysis in Older Patients
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes an alternative to dialysis for older patients with kidney failure. The supplied record does not identify the intervention or provide outcome data.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.summary_3_sentences: An AI analysis found a signal in routine heart scans associated with sudden cardiac death risk and reportedly outperformed conventional screening. Prospective validation is needed before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Stopping statins after 70 may be safer than expected, but there's a catch
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of nearly 1,900 adults older than 70 found few short-term differences after stopping statins among those without prior heart attack or stroke. Higher rates of serious cardiovascular events or death later in follow-up leave uncertainty about longer-term safety.

articles.title: Drugs like Ozempic may help reverse chronic kidney disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Semaglutide was reported to improve kidney function while repairing blood vessels and reducing inflammation. More information is needed to determine whether the findings represent disease reversal and which patients benefit.

articles.title: Major trial challenges how doctors decide who really needs statins
articles.summary_3_sentences: Coronary-calcium imaging produced a similar observed cardiovascular-event rate to conventional risk assessment while recommending statins to fewer people. Patients shown scan-based evidence were more likely to adhere to recommended medication.

articles.title: Gene editing could replace a lifetime of medication, but there's a catch
articles.summary_3_sentences: One-time gene editing could potentially provide long-lasting protection from high cholesterol and cardiovascular disease. Permanent genomic changes also create safety risks that may emerge only after years of follow-up.

articles.title: Your blood pressure could be dangerous even when your numbers look normal
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a small group of brain cells that limits dangerous blood-pressure swings even when average readings appear normal. The mechanism may point to risks missed by standard measurements.

articles.title: Scientists reveal the hidden danger of missing blood pressure medication
articles.summary_3_sentences: In an analysis of more than 91,000 people, consistent use of blood-pressure medication was associated with an 11% reduction in major cardiovascular events. Patients missing many doses showed little or no measurable benefit.

articles.title: New imaging technology reveals previously unseen immune cell patterns in tissue
articles.summary_3_sentences: BCR-MERFISH maps the locations of antibody-producing cell groups within tissue. The technology may help investigate immune responses in infection, autoimmunity, inflammatory disease, and cancer.

articles.title: Flu vaccine effectiveness often weaker than advertised, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: An analysis found influenza vaccines may often provide less protection against infection than the commonly cited 40% to 60% range. Researchers still emphasized that weaker effectiveness does not mean vaccination lacks benefit.

articles.title: Less than half of TikTok videos on RSV prevention offer high-quality info, paper notes
articles.summary_3_sentences: Only 47% of assessed TikTok videos about RSV prevention provided high-quality information. Topics included maternal vaccination and the long-acting infant antibody nirsevimab.

articles.title: Diagnostic & Therapeutic Gaps in Ebola Response
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Bundibugyo virus outbreak exposed gaps in diagnostic capacity and therapeutic response. The article highlights preparedness needs for Ebola-related outbreaks.

articles.title: Cracks in public health grew in 2026
articles.summary_3_sentences: Outbreaks of measles, cyclosporiasis, Ebola, and hantavirus exposed weaknesses in the U.S. public-health response during 2026. The article describes broader problems in preparedness and response capacity.

articles.title: A rare disease reveals a hidden flaw in the immune system
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that malfunctioning immune cells drive a rare severe inflammatory disorder, revising a long-standing explanation of the disease. Existing medicines were proposed as treatments, and one severely affected infant reportedly improved.

articles.title: The U.S. just lost its measles elimination status. What now?
articles.summary_3_sentences: Measles circulated continuously in the United States for more than a year, resulting in loss of elimination status. The article examines the public-health implications of renewed endemic transmission.

articles.title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
articles.summary_3_sentences: Increasing arginine improved immune recognition, reduced colon tumors, and improved viral-infection outcomes in mice. The findings are preclinical and do not establish that arginine supplements treat cancer or infection in people.

articles.title: New Bacterial Infection Emerging in America
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports an emerging bacterial infection in the United States and emphasizes monitoring and precautionary measures. The supplied record does not identify the bacterium or provide case numbers.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden danger of viral infections that vaccines may prevent
articles.summary_3_sentences: Mice recovering from acute viral infection developed lasting spleen changes and weaker subsequent immune responses. Prior vaccination prevented these changes in the mouse model.

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between acorns and lyme disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Long-term ecological research found that mouse abundance and acorn production predicted later increases in tick populations more strongly than deer numbers. The findings may improve forecasting of Lyme disease risk.

articles.title: Microbiome Therapy May Reduce Transplant Infections
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental microbiome therapy may reduce bloodstream infections among stem-cell transplant recipients. The finding supports further study but does not establish routine clinical use.

articles.title: There May Be New Drug Targets for Treating Coronavirus
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified possible new drug targets for evolving coronaviruses. The record does not describe the targets or report clinical testing.

articles.title: Scientists turn viruses into weapons against deadly superbugs
articles.summary_3_sentences: International guidelines were released for personalized phage therapy against antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Early studies reported improvement in 77% of patients and bacterial clearance in 61%, but controlled evidence remains limited.

articles.title: Scientists solve 30-year-old mystery and discover a hidden defense against inflammation
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified an immune mechanism that protects healthy cells from inflammatory damage generated during infection responses. The mechanism may inform future work on cancer and inflammatory diseases.

articles.title: FDA Approves First Antisense Treatment for Hepatitis B
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA approved bepirovirsen, marketed as Hibsago, as the first antisense oligonucleotide treatment for chronic hepatitis B. The record does not provide efficacy or safety details.

articles.title: JAK Inhibitors May Weaken Antiviral Defenses
articles.summary_3_sentences: JAK inhibitors used for inflammatory diseases may weaken antiviral defenses. The finding highlights a possible infection-related tradeoff of immune suppression.

articles.title: Common drugs may help dangerous viruses spread through the body
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research found that JAK inhibitors can suppress genes involved in defense against influenza, COVID-19, and other viral infections. The mechanism may increase vulnerability among patients using these anti-inflammatory drugs.

articles.title: How This Immune System Branch Drives Immune Responses
articles.summary_3_sentences: The CD1 system presents lipid antigens for recognition by T-cell receptors. The work describes a mechanism through which lipid presentation drives immune responses.

articles.title: Major data gap for gut disorders leaves Aotearoa in the dark
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported a shortage of current New Zealand data on common gut disorders, which may affect about one-third of adults. The gap limits planning and assessment of disease burden.

articles.title: Why do farts smell so bad? The secret is brewing in your gut
articles.summary_3_sentences: Sulfur-containing gases produced by gut bacteria are responsible for much of intestinal gas odor. Food composition and bacterial metabolism influence the amount and type of odor produced.

articles.title: A new fiber supplement could help millions suffering from irritable bowel syndrome
articles.summary_3_sentences: A specially designed fiber blend improved gut health and gut-related anxiety in people with IBS without worsening bloating or pain. It also produced rapid changes in gut bacteria.

articles.title: Blood Shows IBD Risk 10 Years Before Diagnosis
articles.summary_3_sentences: Blood antibody profiles may reveal inflammatory bowel disease risk as long as 10 years before diagnosis. Prospective validation is needed before these patterns can be used for screening.

articles.title: When your gut bacteria run out of fiber, they may start eating your gut lining
articles.summary_3_sentences: When dietary fiber is scarce, gut bacteria can consume intestinal mucus and produce potentially harmful compounds. Fiber and proteins from plant foods shifted microbial metabolism toward more beneficial products.

articles.title: Vitamin D improves IBD immune and gut bacteria communication
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research examined how vitamin D affects communication between the immune system and gut bacteria in inflammatory bowel disease. Vitamin D deficiency is common in IBD, but whether it contributes causally remains unresolved.

articles.title: IBD-Linked Antibody Changes May Precede Diagnosis by Years
articles.summary_3_sentences: IBD-associated antibody changes were detectable in blood as long as 10 years before diagnosis. The patterns may offer information about early disease development.

articles.title: IBD Colonoscopy Experience Linked to Higher Polyp Detection
articles.summary_3_sentences: Greater clinician experience with IBD colonoscopy was associated with higher polyp detection. Longer examination time and dye-enhanced visibility were also identified as potentially helpful.

articles.title: Scientists solve a 30-year mystery behind inflammatory bowel disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified antibodies that disable a natural immune mechanism for controlling inflammation in some cases of IBD. The discovery may support more precise diagnosis and targeted treatment.

articles.title: IBD-like inflammation leaves lasting mark on the colon
articles.summary_3_sentences: IBD-like inflammation was reported to leave persistent changes in the colon after an inflammatory episode. The finding may help explain features of remission and recurrence.

articles.title: Your blood could reveal inflammatory bowel disease 10 years before diagnosis
articles.summary_3_sentences: Distinct blood-antibody patterns were detectable as long as 10 years before Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis diagnosis. Some patterns also distinguished people who later developed more complicated disease.

articles.title: Researchers uncover the mechanisms of adhesion formation after thoracic surgery
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers created an animal model of pleural adhesions after thoracic surgery and investigated the cells and signaling pathways involved. The preclinical work aims to identify ways to prevent adhesions before repeat operations.

articles.title: Patients give dental implants high marks after 40 years
articles.summary_3_sentences: Patients remained highly satisfied with dental implant function nearly 40 years after treatment. Satisfaction with appearance was more variable.

articles.title: AI Could Transform Dermatology, but Bias Remains
articles.summary_3_sentences: Artificial intelligence may improve diagnosis and treatment of skin disorders. Bias remains a major limitation that could produce unequal performance across patient groups.

articles.title: Dietary Fat Metabolite Linked to Chronic Itch
articles.summary_3_sentences: A metabolite produced from a common dietary fat was linked with chronic itch and skin inflammation. The finding suggests a metabolic pathway for further study.

articles.title: A common osteoporosis drug blocked spinal damage in a surprising new study
articles.summary_3_sentences: An osteoporosis drug prevented damaging mineral buildup in zebrafish spines in a study of spinal degeneration. The result is preclinical and does not establish treatment for human back pain.

articles.title: Exercise after ACL surgery may protect knees from early osteoarthritis
articles.summary_3_sentences: A four-month supervised exercise program after ACL reconstruction improved pain, strength, and quality of life without damaging knee cartilage. The findings support structured rehabilitation after surgery.

articles.title: Without this protein, damaged muscle fills with fat and scar tissue
articles.summary_3_sentences: TRF2 helped muscle stem cells maintain their identity and repair damaged muscle in mice. Removing it caused fat and scar accumulation and accelerated muscular dystrophy, making the findings preclinical.

articles.title: Get Pumped: Hypertrophy Reveals a New Muscle Nucleus Type
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research on skeletal-muscle hypertrophy identified a previously unreported type of muscle nucleus. The finding adds detail to the cellular biology of muscle growth.

articles.title: The mystery of how hair knows where to grow may finally be solved
articles.summary_3_sentences: Hair-follicle patterns may emerge from cells following relatively simple chemical signals. The finding challenges a long-standing explanation for how mammalian hair patterns form.

articles.title: Vitamin D Derivative Shows Promise for Psoriasis
articles.summary_3_sentences: Pantethine, a vitamin B5 derivative, was reported to alleviate psoriasis symptoms. The supplied record does not describe the study design or level of clinical evidence.

articles.title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Increased Nail Disorders
articles.summary_3_sentences: GLP-1 receptor agonists were associated with a higher prevalence of nail disorders. The potential dermatological adverse effect requires additional investigation.

articles.title: A surprising discovery could help aging muscles repair themselves
articles.summary_3_sentences: A compound strengthened the receptor binding and chemical stability of the muscle-repair protein HGF. Early mouse experiments suggest potential for age-related muscle loss, but the work remains preclinical.

articles.title: Scientists discover why chronic back pain feels so personal
articles.summary_3_sentences: Movement-triggered chronic back pain activated a brain network involved in self-awareness and memory, unlike typical acute pain. The finding may help explain why prior experience and anticipation influence chronic pain.

articles.title: Scientists discover that cranberry juice may help fight tooth decay
articles.summary_3_sentences: Pure unsweetened cranberry juice slowed dental-plaque bacterial regrowth and reduced acid production in laboratory research. Proanthocyanidins may mediate the effect, but clinical prevention of cavities was not demonstrated.

articles.title: Prebiotic Fiber May Ease Knee Arthritis Pain
articles.summary_3_sentences: The prebiotic fiber inulin was reported to reduce knee osteoarthritis pain and improve muscle strength. The supplied record does not provide trial details.

articles.title: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength
articles.summary_3_sentences: A clinical trial found that daily prebiotic fiber reduced knee osteoarthritis pain, improved muscle strength, and decreased pain sensitivity. Changes in gut bacteria and GLP-1 signaling may contribute.

articles.title: A simple liquid can stop cavities without drilling, major study confirms
articles.summary_3_sentences: A major pediatric trial found that a liquid painted onto teeth could arrest cavities without drilling or anesthesia. The inexpensive treatment may reduce the need for invasive dental procedures.

articles.title: A Expectant Mother's Environment influences Postnatal Psychiatric Predisposition
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article proposes that maternal diet, exposures, and psychological environment can influence fetal development through epigenetic changes. The supplied record does not quantify later psychiatric risk or establish causality.

articles.title: The libido drug women want is testosterone
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article examines testosterone as a possible treatment for low sexual desire in women. The supplied record does not provide efficacy, safety, or regulatory details.

articles.title: U.S. demand for menopause hormone therapy has more than doubled recently
articles.summary_3_sentences: U.S. pharmacy data showed that menopause hormone-therapy use among women ages 40 to 74 more than doubled from 2023 to 2026. The finding documents demand rather than treatment effectiveness or safety.

articles.title: Fetal Cells in Mom's Blood Could Improve Prenatal Testing
articles.summary_3_sentences: Fetal cells circulating in maternal blood may provide information for prenatal screening through a blood draw. The approach could reduce reliance on invasive tests but remains under development.

articles.title: Most transgender youth satisfied after choosing hormone therapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a large U.S. study, 97% of transgender and gender-diverse young people said hormone therapy was the right decision. The finding measures satisfaction with the treatment choice.

articles.title: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy
articles.summary_3_sentences: Early GLP-1 drug exposure was not associated with increased pregnancy complications when prescribed for weight loss but was associated with premature birth when prescribed for diabetes. Researchers cautioned that diabetes itself may explain the difference and that pregnancy safety remains uncertain.

articles.title: Animal vs. plant protein reveals a surprising testosterone divide
articles.summary_3_sentences: Among more than 2,500 men, higher animal-protein intake, especially dairy, was associated with lower testosterone, while plant protein was associated with higher levels. The observational relationship does not establish that protein source changes testosterone.

topic_groups.topic: Research Tools, Biotechnology and Drug Policy

articles.title: Regeneron Gained FDA Approval for RNAi Treatment Livsayis
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA approved Regeneron's RNA-interference therapy Livsayis. The supplied record does not specify the indication, trial evidence, or approved population.

articles.title: Blackstone Life Sciences Funds Pfizer's Obesity Drug Program
articles.summary_3_sentences: Blackstone Life Sciences will provide $1.5 billion for Pfizer's obesity-drug development program. The funding is intended to support 10 related projects or activities.

articles.title: Akagera Secures $7.8M for mRNA TB Vaccine
articles.summary_3_sentences: Akagera Medicines received $7.8 million from the Gates Foundation to develop an experimental mRNA tuberculosis vaccine. The record reports funding rather than clinical results.

articles.title: Repurposing AI tool to reveal mitochondrial protein functions
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers repurposed an AI tool to investigate functions of poorly characterized mitochondrial proteins. The work addresses an unresolved portion of the mitochondrial proteome.

articles.title: New Open-Source Workflow Maps Thousands of Proteins Inside Tissues
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers developed an open-source workflow combining tissue imaging with molecular analysis to map thousands of proteins. The platform is intended to make spatial proteomic analysis more accessible.

articles.title: Novel Design Improves Small Molecule Detection
articles.summary_3_sentences: A new laboratory design was reported to improve detection of small molecules in biological samples. Such detection may support biomarker analysis and diagnosis.

articles.title: Beam Therapeutics Sues YolTech Therapeutics and Serapha Bio
articles.summary_3_sentences: Beam Therapeutics filed litigation against YolTech Therapeutics and its U.S. partner Serapha Bio. The dispute involves companies working in gene editing rather than a new laboratory or clinical result.

articles.title: Timing and spatial CRISPR control in mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers demonstrated temporal and spatial control of CRISPR activity in mice, including gene editing limited to one brain hemisphere. The work may support more precise preclinical experiments.

articles.title: Novel Proteins Identified in Dataset Advances Therapeutic Development
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified previously uncharacterized proteins in a dataset intended to support therapeutic development. The record does not identify the diseases, targets, or validation methods.

articles.title: DNA’s secret sunscreen may have helped life survive on early Earth
articles.summary_3_sentences: A component of DNA may convert ultraviolet damage into a form that is easier to repair. The mechanism could help explain how early life endured intense UV radiation.

articles.title: A 50-year-old theory about evolution may have been wrong all along
articles.summary_3_sentences: Mutation analyses in bacteria and yeast found no evidence that essential genes mutate less often than other genes. Earlier findings may have confused mutation rates with removal of harmful variants by natural selection.

articles.title: Something strange is living beneath the skin of deep-sea pigs
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists found a bacterium with a tiny genome living beneath the skin of deep-sea sea pigs. Much of its genome encodes surface proteins, suggesting strong dependence on its host.

articles.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
articles.summary_3_sentences: Crows identified the direction of moving visual patterns in about 235 milliseconds, roughly twice as fast as humans and monkeys in the reported task. They maintained high accuracy despite the speed.

articles.title: A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets
articles.summary_3_sentences: A tropical butterfly previously treated as one species was found to comprise three nearly identical species. DNA and ultraviolet wing patterns revealed the differences.

articles.title: Scientists discover that necks didn't evolve for the reason we thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: Early land vertebrates appear to have had stiff necks, challenging the idea that necks evolved primarily to turn the head. Necks may instead have emerged alongside changes supporting movement with front limbs.

articles.title: Scientists find deadly virus DNA hidden in 1,000-year-old manuscripts
articles.summary_3_sentences: Historic parchment manuscripts contained DNA from a sheep virus with a history extending more than 3,700 years. The viral genome appears to have changed little, making parchment a record of ancient animal disease.

articles.title: Scientists just found dinosaur blood that survived 115 million years
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported chemically confirmed traces of blood-related material in 115-million-year-old dinosaur bones. The preservation may provide new information about dinosaur physiology and biomolecular survival.

articles.title: Five-inch-long beetle larvae are quietly destroying blueberry roots
articles.summary_3_sentences: DNA analysis identified the beetle species whose large larvae have been damaging blueberry roots in North Carolina. The finding resolves a long-running agricultural pest mystery.

articles.title: Scientists discover a bacterial defense so strange they thought it was broken
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a bacterial defense that produces the DNA needed to activate a lethal toxin only after viral infection begins. The infected bacterium then self-destructs, limiting viral spread.

articles.title: New Evidence Suggests that Dr. Rosalind Franklin First Recognized the DNA Double Helix
articles.summary_3_sentences: New historical evidence suggests Rosalind Franklin recognized the DNA double-helix structure before she was traditionally credited with doing so. The article contributes to continuing reassessment of the 1953 discovery.

articles.title: Microplastics may be more dangerous than we thought. Scientists just discovered why
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that microplastics interacting with water can generate reactive molecules capable of damaging cells and tissues. The mechanism may help explain reported health associations, but it does not establish specific disease risks in people.

articles.title: The Influence of Steroid Hormones on the Aquatic Ecosystem
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article examines how steroid hormones and other chemical pollutants affect aquatic ecosystems. The reported concern is increased harm and mortality among marine organisms.

articles.title: Toxic secrets are hiding in Arctic ice
articles.summary_3_sentences: Arctic ice cores preserved arsenic, lead, and other heavy metals traced to historic mining and smelting in Montana. The record demonstrates long-range transport and persistence of industrial pollution.
